premise.claim: On base, the four sites named in issue #6220 iterate Go maps unsorted when building NodeSelector MatchExpressions / scheduling terms, producing non-deterministic output order across calls for multi-key selectors or multi-runtime pods.
premise.evidence: results/base-run.txt and results/base-volume-run.txt: 5 harness tests fail on base with 4-6 distinct orderings observed (500/300/80/60 iterations per site). Same tests pass on head (results/head-run.txt, results/head-volume-run.txt).

findings.evidence: Premise/fix verification: all 5 contract tests red on base (multiple orderings), green on head (single sorted ordering).

Code-path reasoning: pkg/webhook/plugins/requirenodewithfuse/require_node_with_fuse.go Mutate() iterates runtimeInfos (a map) at line ~61, so the ORDER of the per-runtime NodeSelectorTerms remains random; the PR only sorts MatchExpressions within each term. Scheduling semantics unchanged (terms are OR'ed), so non-blocking. No harness test: a canary asserting randomness would be flaky by construction.

Code-path reasoning: pkg/dataflow/helper.go (~line 50) iterates the pod annotations map unsorted when appending NodeSelectorRequirements - the same nondeterminism class as issue #6220, but not one of the sites it enumerates. Out of the PR's stated scope; track separately.

pkg/utils/affinity_test.go deterministic_order_over_repeated_calls computes expected := ToNodeSelectorRequirements(multi) from the function under test, so it only detects cross-call randomness, not unsortedness; the table test multiple_entries_sorted is what actually pins the order. Test-quality nit.
